Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Combat feedback

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Cavecrawl now presents its replayed player-hit, dweller-hit, player-death and dweller-death occurrences through replay/view.Cues. The common frontend covers both server motion and the separately runnable owner-motion profile.

Player death emits the original red pyre color; slain dwellers emit purple sparks; player and dweller hits emit yellow sparks and a red-to-white 0.3-second flash. The emitter matches the original authored values: 12 particles, 0.4-second particle lifetime, one shot, full explosiveness, 180-degree spread and speed 40–90. Detached burst nodes live for 0.8 seconds under Stage. Their saved occurrence position survives entity removal. The copied avatar's dormant Pyre node remains non-emitting.

Confirmation does not restart particles. Correction moves an active burst; cancellation hides and removes it. Consumed IDs remain remembered after expiry or cancellation. Late joins seed from the snapshot baseline without manufacturing bursts from old corpses. Epoch changes and floor/run transitions clear prior visuals. Leaving destroys both nodes and bookkeeping. The presentation layer does not change gameplay/save/wire schemas; C9/O3 separately version the new simulation impact events.

The player Hit occurrence also covers dweller bites; these now receive the same flash/sparks. The original explicit contact renderer was tied to rock tracers, so this broader damage feedback is a recorded presentation difference.

C9/O3 adds all dweller contacts, retaining their target generation for flashes and detached positions for sparks. Rock views now move between fixed simulation ticks, while render-time cast/contact prediction remains a separate difference from Kit. Particle paths are cosmetic and are not part of deterministic state or a pixel-equality guarantee.
